FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by Meteorological Instruments Sectional Committee had been approved by the Light Mechanical Engineering Division Council. This standard was originally published been incorporated: a) b) C) cl) Operating secondary Reference to Indian Wind speed in kmph Pig. 4 connection of modified. in 1978. In this revision the following changes have

voltage of maximum 110 V AC 50 HZ has been incorporated. Standards for standard cabinet has been incorporated. has been included along with speed in knots. wind panel anemometer and windvane ( selsyn system ) has been

The accurate measurement of wind speed and direction is of great importance in meteorological transport, shipping, engineering and in research and practice, as well as in aviation, agriculture, other fields. The simplest and most common method of measuring these two parameters near the ground is by the use of direct reading anemometers ( see IS 5912 : 1970 ) and windvanes ( see IS 5799 : 1970 ). Remote indicating electrical anemometers and windvanes are also extensively used, particularly at some of the aeronautical meteorological stations, for the measurement of wind speed and direction at distant locations ( see IS 6871 : 1992 ). Distant indicating and recording wind equipments are in use at some important meteorological stations and specially at the more important aeronautical meteorological stations. With the increasing use and manufacture in the country of such equipment, known by the short name of electrical anemographs, the formulation of an Indian Standard Specification for the equipment has become necessary. This standard has, therefore, wind speed and direction anemograph. been prepared in the interest of accuracy of the measurement of and of standardization in the manufacture of the electrical

In the formulation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the requirements laid Geneva, in addition to the special requiredown by the World Meteorological Organization, ments obtained in this country. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

IS 8754 : 1992

Indian Standard

ELECTRICAL ANEMOGRAPH-SPECIFICATION
( First Revision )
1 SCOPE

This standard specifies the requirements for the electrical anemogtaph assembly, consisting an electrical of an electrical anemometer, windvane, with remote-indicating wind speed and direction indicators and recorders. 2 REFERENCES The following Indian Standards adjuncts to this standard:
IS No.

are necessary

3.3 The anemometer is the cup generator type and consists of a three cup rotor assembly which drives a multipole permanent magnet rotor inside a stator consisting of coils wound on a laminated core. The alternating current generated is rectified and measured on a dc voltmeter. The voltage and frequency of the alternating current generated are nearly proportional to the wind speed which is directly read on the wind speed indicator. It is also recorded on a moving coil dc milliampere roll chart recorder. 3.4 The electrical windvane consists of a vane assembly with its spindle coupled to a magslip selsyn transmitting motor and a weather-proof housing and the wind direction indicator containing a magslip receiving motor, both transmitter and receiver having similar electrical components. The windvane is operated by a secondary voltage of maximum 110 V AC 50 Hz supply from a Transformer Unit connected to 230 V AC 50 Hz mains. The movements of the transmitter rotor are followed by the receiver rotor and indicated by a pointer attached to the rotor-shaft of the receiving motor located in the wind indicator. A third magslip receiving motor connected in parallel operates the wind direction recorder in which the motor is mechanically linked to a recording pen through a pinion and gear assembly. * 3.5 The indicator unit consists of a metal cabinet on which are mounted the wind speed and wind direction indicators. A transformer and two toggle switches in the front panel, control the connection between the sensors and the indicating meters. A two-pin plug for the 230 V ac mains and an octal socket for the lead wires from the sensors are provided at the back of the cabinet.
NOTE - If standard cabinets are required, 1979 and IS 9609 : 1980 may be referred. IS 2419 :

3 DESCRIPTION
3.1 The electrical

anemograph remotely indicates and records the instantaneous values of wind speed and direction as well as the various gust parameters of operational significance, namely, the maximum and minimum speed of the gust along with its duration.

3.2 It consists of the electrical anemometer a,id windvane mounted on a supporting mast assemblv and electricallv connected bv means of cable-s to the wind speed and direct& indicaters and recorders, located at a distance from the wind sensors. 1

an internal diameter of exactly 127.0 mm and be semiconical in shape with beaded edges. Any alteration in the shape or dimensions of the cup and the cup arm is likely to result in a departure from the desired ratio between the cup rotor revolutio:l and true wind speed. 6.1.2 The generator housing shall be weatherproof. A one-metre length of twin core PVC sheathed cable shall be provided, one end of which shall be connected to the terminals of the generator in such a way that no short-circuiting ( due to moisture or any other cause ) may occur while at the same time, inspection of the mechanism is possible without detaching the cable. 6.1.3 The main shaft shall rotate in two ball bearings, one at the top and the other at the bottom. The bearings shall be adequately enclosed, lubricated and protected from dust and moisture. 6.1.4 The rotor shall be permanent multi-pole magnet, fully magnetized, and fixed to the main shaft through an adjusting sleeve to facilitate correct adjustment of the position of the rotor. 6.1.5 The stator stampings shall be riveted together within two end plates of mild steel. The coils shall be wound over their projections and connected in series. The complete stator with coils shall be mounted securely on the base casting on three pillars. 6.1.6 The terminal voltage of the generator shall be 10 000 f 0.025 volts at 1 000 rev/min, when supplying a total of 5 mA to a circuit having negligible inductance at a temperature of 18 f 2�C. 6.2 Electrical

Windvane

6.1.7 The electrical resistances of the generator and indicators shall be such that one, two or three indicators may be used in parallel with one generator without affecting their accuracy of indication, provided the total resistance of each core of the cable between the generator and indicator does not exceed 10 ohms. 6.1.8 In order to allow the interchangeability between different generator and indicator units, the design of cup rotor, generator and indicator shall be so selected that the following relationship is obtained:
Speed of Rotation Wind Speed Wind Speed

6.2.1 The fin of the windvane shall be securely fixed at right angles to the horizontal arm at one end. The other end shall have a counterweight fixed in such a way that the complete assembly is well-balanced about the central spindle. The horizontal arm shall be straight and shall have no relative movement with respect to the spindle. 6.2.2 The dust cover shall have a locking pin projecting up, to lock it to the cone of the horizontal arm. The central hole in the dust cover shall take the spindle snugly without play. The dust cover shall be locked to the spindle by a steel pin. 6.2.3 The spindle bearing support shall hold the ball bearing tightly. It shall have a hole at the base to serve as a bearing for the spindle. It shall also have four threaded holes near the base at right angles to its axis, for the four direction rods. Exactly below one of these holes, the letter `N' shall be marked to facilitate proper orientation of the windvane. The spindle bearing support shall rest on and be securely fixed to the main housing. It shall hold the transmitter support at the bottom. 6.2.4 The housing for the transmitter shall be fixed to the base of the spindle bearing support. The lower portion of the housing shall be shaped in such a way that the entire windvane can be clamped to a 50 mm galvanized iron pipe firmly. The housing shall be provided with a hole at the base for the lead wires to come out through a bush.

The split bar holding the spindle shall be held inside the flexible coupling by two clips.

6.2.9 The flexible coupling shall be made of two brass channels soldered at right ahgles to each other. The lower channel shall have grooves cut in it to expose the screws fixing the transmitter shaft to the split bar. A steel pin shall be riveted at one end of the lower channel to serve as a stop for the split bar. 6.2.10 The four direction rods shall be screwed into the threaded holes near the base of the spindle bearing support. The other ends of the rods carry the direction letter N, S, E and W. Each rod shall be provided with a locking nut. 6.2.11 The windvane shall be correctly aligned with the indicator such that the direction indicated by vane agrees with that of the pointer of the indicator. 6.3 Wind Indicator
6.3.1 The wind speed indicator

scale having the full range 0 to 100 knots with a pointer movement of approximately 270" or two scales having ranges of 0 to 20 knots and 0 to 100 knots with a pointer movement of approximately 90". Full range deflection in the two scales shall be 1.04 volts for the 0 to 20 knots scale and 9.4 volts for the 0 to 100 knots scale with the range selection being done by a spring loaded switch. Full range deflection for the single scale shall be for 9.4 volts. The electrical resistance of the indicator shall be such that one, two or three indicators may be used in parallel with one generator anemometer without affecting the accuracy of the indication. The indicator shall show the true speed when the total resistance of each core of the cable between the generator and the indicator does not exceed 10 ohms. The scale shall be so laid out that the readable value is not less than 0.5 knot. 6.3.2 The be that it indicator true wind prescribed design of the speed indicator shall shall be possible to interchange the and/or generator to obtain the speed within the limits of accuracy in this standard.

6.3.3 The wind drrection indicator shall consist of a magslip receiver motor operating on 501 110 V ac supply obtained from a transformer connected to the 230 volts ac mains. The pointer attached to the shaft of the motor shall traverse over a dial graduated for every 5" position of the compass. The indicator shall

IS a154 : 1992 be capable of denoting accurately the wind direction when connected to its transmitter with a suitable cable, the resistance of each of the five cores being less than 10 ohms. The design shall be such that the accuracy of indication of direction shall be within the limits prescribed in this standard even when two indicators and one recorder are connected in parallel to the same transmitter. 6.3.4 Both the front and rear panels of the cabinet shall be detachable. The front panel shall be designed to take in the speed and direction indicator dials, a pilot lamp and two spring loaded toggle switches. The rear panel shall be perforated for ventilation and shall hold a flush mounting two pin plug for the mains and flush mounting octal socket for the sensors. The cabinet shall contain a transformer which shall be rated for a continuous current of 2.5 A with secondary tappings for 50 V, 110 V and 6 V. 6.3.5 The cabinet shall be made to the smallest convenient size depending upon the dimensions of the various components used. The various electrical connections shall be firmly made with solder using PVC insulated wires of different colour. The exposed portions of the bare wires shall be adequately covered with fibre glass sleeving to avoid possibility of shortcircuiting anywhere. 6.3.6 The general wiring diagram of the wind indicator and its connections to the sensors shall be as shown in Fig. 4. 6.4 Wind Speed Recorder 6.4.1 The wind speed recorder shall be a moving coil dc milliampere roll-chart recorder with a measuring range from 0 to 1.0 mA and an internal impedence of 1 500 ohms, graduated to record wind speeds up to 100 knots or full scale deflection. The output from the sensor be dropped through suitable resistances, rectified, smoothend and fed to the moving coil of the recorder. 6.4.2 The recorder shall give a continuous record of the wind speed on a roll chart by means of a capillary pen writing with ink on paper. 6.4.3 The chart drive of the recorder shall be operated by a 230 volts, 50 Hz self starting synchronous motor. The chart speed shall be 15 mm/h and 60 mm/h by manual change of gears. 7 6.4.4 The recorder shall racy of f 2 percent. have an overall accuwith of its

6.4.5 The recorder shall be provided means to shift and adjust the position zero.

6.4.6 The measuring circuit of the recorder shall have the temperature coefficient as near to zero as possible and the total errors of the recording apparatus shall not exceed f 2 percent. 6.4.7 An additional facility of a selector switch shall be provided to choose either of the following two ranges: 0 to 0 to 100 knots 50 knots

6.5 Wind Direction Recorder 6.5.1 The wind director recorder shall be designed to record with a single pen, the wind direction, irrespective of the sense of rotation of the vane. It shall consist of a magslip motor, linked to the recorder pen either mechanically or electrically, so that the pen records faithfully the movement of the wind vane. The design shall incorporate means to record both the veering and backing of the wind from any direction. The pen traverse shall be either or 360" with North ( 360� ) at either end, through 90", 1800 and 270" or for 7200 with North ( 360" ) both at either ends as well as in the centre. 6.5.2 The recorder shall give a continuous record of the wind direction on a roll chart by means of a capillary pen writing with ink on paper. 6.5.3 The chart drive of the recorder shall be operated by a 230 volts, 50 Hz self-starting synchronous motor. The chart speed and other characteristics of the recorder shall be as laid down in 6.4.3 to 6.4.6.

6.6 Recorder Chart 6.6.1 The chart be of the roll type suitable for the recorder with which it is to be used. 6.6.2 The type indicated in Fig. 5 and designated WSI shall be acceptable for recording the wind speed, while the type indicated in Fig. 6 and designated WDI shall be acceptable for recording the wind direction.

6.6.3 The charts shall have a minimum length of 15 metres and a graduated width of 89 mm, for wind speed and 89 mm for wind direction. 6.6.4 The chart for wind speed WS1 shall be divided along its length into 47 divisions and shall have printed on it, curved lines corresponding to hours, the time scale being equal to 15 mm/h. The time arcs shall have a radius of 165 mm and shall appropriately be figured from O-24 along the longitudinal edge the figures being repeated for each day. Along the curved lines shall be entered from the lefthand side the set of figures 100, 80, 60, 40 and 20, at intervals of ten longitudinal divisions, the set of figures being spaced 120 mm apart. There shall be five longitudinal divisions after the figure 20, the fifth division corresponding to wind speed of 10 knots and one longitudinal division corresponding to 5 knots between the 10 knots line and the 0 knot line. Every line responding to 10 knots and multiples thereof shall be thicker, but the thickness shall not exceed O-2 mm. The other lines shall be fine, thin and, uniform. The spacing of the main longitudinal divisions shall be as follows:
Line Corresponding Speed to Distant from the `0' Knot Line

The thin lines corresponding to 5 knots and those corresponding to every 2 knots above the 10 knots line, shalI all be equispaced within the space available between the relevant thickened lines. 6.6.5 The chart for wind direction WDI shall be divided along its length into either 24 or 48 equal divisions corresponding to pen traverse of 360" or 720' respectively. It shall have printed on it curved lines corresponding to hours, the time scale being equal to at least 15 mm/h. The hour lines shall appropriately be figured from 0 to 24 along the longitudinal edge. Along the curved lines shall be entered from left-hand side the following figures at intervals of six longitudinal divisions: 360, 90, 180, 270 and 360 for chart having 24 longitudinal divisions or 360, 90, 180, 270, 360, 90, 180, 270 and 360 for chart having 48 longitudinal divisions. The set of figures shall be spaced 120 mm apart. Alternating with the above set of figures, another set of figures, shall also be entered 120 mm apart from one another, which shall indicate the cardinal directions corresponding to the degrees mentioned above, like N for 360", E for 90", S for 180" and W for 270". 6.6.6 The chart shall be printed on thin white paper on which the recording ink shall not spread or show tendency to feather. 6.7 Recorders and charts manufactured as per IS 6236 i 1971 and IS 9347 : 1979 are also acceptable. 7 WORKMANSHIP

of the anemometer shall be such that the cups start rotating at low wind speeds not exceeding 3 knots. The rotation of the cup assembly shall be smooth and free from friction. The shaft shall be straight and suffi_ ciently strong so as not to bend or get deformed even under extreme working conditions. The bearings of the generator shaft shall be adequately lubricated and protected from weather. The rotor shall not touch or foul the stator at any time. The external surfaces of the instrument shall be painted with under coat ( see IS 2074 : 1979 ) and finishing paint ( see IS 2932 : 1974 ). All rotating parts shall be well polished. The stator shall be coated with shellac. 7.2 The workmanship of the windvane shall be such that the vane moves with minimum friction and indicates changes in direction of the magnitude of 2". As in the anemometer, all rotating parts in the windvane shall be well polished and the external surfaces painted with

IS 8754 : 1992

undercoat ( see IS 2074 : 1979 ) and finishing paint (see IS 2932 : 1974 ). The coupling between the spindle shaft and the transmitter shaft shall be rigid without any play. The split bars, flexible coupling and the mounting and terminal block plate shall have a dull plating of nickle. The figurings on the terminal block plate shall be filled with red paint, as also the letter `N' marked on the bottom of the spindle bearing support. The direction letters N, S, E and W shall be painted red. 7.3 The wind indicator shall have a fine finish. The inscriptions on the front penal shall be engraved and filled in with paint easily distinguishable from the rest of the cabinet. 7.4 The workmanship and finish of the two recorders shall also be the best acceptable in scientific and research laboratories. They shall be capable of continuous trouble-free operation for lcng periods extending up to 10 years and more. 7.5 All the electrical connections shall be made neatly using minimum amount of solder while at the same time ensuring strength and permanence of contact. The electrical junctions shall be suitably protected by glass fibre sleevings and wax coating to prevent malfunctioning of the electrical circuit -due to high humidity and presence of water vapour. 8 TESTS AND TOLERANCES 8.1 Cup Generator

8.1.4 The cup rotor sball begin t$ revolve from rest in a wind speed not exceeding 3 knots. 8.2 Windvane The rotating parts of the windvane shall be accurately balanced when tested in a room free from draughts. 8.3 Wind Indicator
8.3.1

The wind speed indicator shall give full scale deflection for 5mA dc. The pointer shall move freely.

8.3.2 The wind direction indicator shall be so adjusted to its transmitter that the pointer indicates North ( 360' ) when the balancing weight of the windvane points in the direction of the letter `N' marked on the spindle bearing support of the windvane. The adjustment shall be correct to within ~1". 8.3.3 The indicator shah be capable of following all the minute oscillations of the windvane such that the indicated direction agrees with true direction with an accuracy of &2". 8.4 Wind Recorders Both the speed and direction ret .ders shall agree tith the respective indicators within 0.5 knot for speed and &2" for direction. 9 MARKING
9.1 Marking AND PACKING

8.1.1 The rotating parts of the generator auemometer shall be accurately balanced and the cup arms shall be securely held in their sockets in the central spider casting at speeds up to 1000 rev/min. The test for balancing of the cups shall be carried out inside a room free from draughts before attaching the magnet to the shaft. While carrying out the test for balancing of the cups, with spindle held in horizontal position, the cups shall not show bias to any particular position.

8.1.2 To ensure sufficient freedom of the ball bearings, the cups when set revolving at one revolution per second for 30 seconds in the direction they would normally rotate in wind shall continue to be in motion for at least 90 seconds before commg to rest. This test shall also be conducted inside a room free from draughts and before the magnet is fixed to the shaft. 8.1.3 The anemometer shall be such that when connected to the indicator the indicated speed

Standard Mark The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standurdr Act, 2986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Marb on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producero may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
